children.name: Alloschemone inopinata
children.description: Alloschemone inopinata is a species of flowering plant in the genus Alloschemone of the arum family Araceae.

children.name: Alloschemone occidentalis
children.description: Alloschemone occidentalis is a flowering plant in genus Alloschemone of the arum family Araceae.

children.name: Rhaphidophora

children.name: Rhaphidophora amplissimia Schott, 1863
children.description: Rhaphidophora amplissimia Schott, 1863 is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora angustata Schott
children.description: A frequently very high-climbing species unmistakable by the scattered fans of large bright-green soft-textured litter-trapping leaves carried on short stout shoots and held at about 90º to the ± leafless main stem. The large slender inflorescences arise from these fans.

children.name: Rhaphidophora angustiloba Ridl.
children.description: Rhaphidophora angustiloba Ridl. is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora apiculata Atderwer.
children.description: Rhaphidophora apiculata Atderwer. is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora araea P.C.Boyce
children.description: Peduncle subequalling or exceeding petioles, spathe 4-5 cm, spadix 2.4-3.2 cm, stipitate. Plant terrestrial, perhaps occasionally rheophytic. Sumatera (endemic)

children.name: Rhaphidophora australasica F.M.Bailey
children.description: Rhaphidophora australasica F.M.Bailey (needle berry) is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora balgooyi P.C.Boyce
children.description: Spadix at anthesis 11--15 cm long; stigma round, flat. Maluku (Ternate, Buru - endemic) Described by Alderwerelt as a robust form of R. ternatensis, R. balgooyi differs in lacking cataphyll, prophyll and petiolar sheath fibres, in the significantly less prominent primary lateral leaf venation, the considerably larger spadix and flat stigmas. Confusion with

children.name: Rhaphidophora banosensis P.C.Boyce
children.description: Immediately identifiable by the long, narrow falcate leaf lamina and relatively short petiole.

children.name: Rhaphidophora bogneri P.C.Boyce & Haigh
children.description: The native range of this species is Cameroon to Gabon. It is a liana and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora bonii Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Caudex teres 1,2 – 1,6 cm crassus internodiis 1,4-3 cm longis. Foliorum petiolus tenuis 6-8 cm longus ad geniculum ca. 8 mm longum supra profundiuscule canaliculatum usque vagina angusta membranacea mox dilacerata instructus, lamina tenuiter coriacea suboblique oblonga apice cuspidato-acuminata basi acuta, 2,2-3 dm longa, 0,8- 1dm lata, paullum inaequilatera, altero latere fere ¼ latiore, nervis lateralibus I. numerosis angulo ca. 75º a costa abeuntibus marginem versus leviter arcuatim adscen

children.name: Rhaphidophora brevispathacea Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Distinctive by the long pendent stems with much abbreviated, netting-sheathed flowering shoots and a small, marcescent spathe. Rhaphidophora stolleana shares the habit of long pendent stems with abbreviated of inflorescence-bearing shoots arising in the leaf axils, but is readily distinguished by a much longer spathe (c. 10.2 cm long) and spadix (c. 8 cm long). To date R. brevispathacea is known

children.name: Rhaphidophora bulusanensis Elmer ex Merr.
children.description: Rhaphidophora bulusanensis Elmer ex Merr. is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora calophylla Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is E. Himalaya to China (Yunnan) and Nicobar Is.. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora corneri P.C.Boyce
children.description: The manner of inflorescence production in R. corneri is unique in the genus. The inflorescences arise sequentially from an elongated reiterative floral sympodium on the tips of (probably) plagiotropic free lateral shoots with each new inflorescence carried some distance from that preceding. The specimen studied bears the scars of several inflorescences together with two developing inflorescences at different stages of maturity, suggesting that

children.name: Rhaphidophora crassicaulis Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Lianas. Branches dorsiventrally compressed, to 3cm in diam., internodes short. Leaf blade ovate in outline, 30–55 × 22–36cm, leathery, base obtuse, apex acute, pinnately divided; pinnae 6–10 or more per side, reaching midrib or nearly so, linear-falcate, base decurrent, apex truncate; primary lateral veins usually 2–4, equally strong, parallel, along midrib with perforations (8–20 × 2–5mm), pinnae at middle of leaf 15–21 × 1–5cm. Inflorescences terminal on lateral branches, solitary, erect; p

children.name: Rhaphidophora cravenschoddeana P.C.Boyce
children.description: Easily confused with Rhaphidophora intonsa (also with large inflorescences and fibrous shoot tips) but separated by the simple, not netted, fibres, thinner-textured leaf lamina with, on the abaxial surface, a conspicuously raised midrib and much more pronounced differentiation between the primary lateral and interprimary veins, and by the long-exserted anthers.

children.name: Rhaphidophora cretosa P.C.Boyce
children.description: Leaf lamina non-falcate, 5.5--16 x 2--5 cm, thinly coriaceous with veins not particularly prominent. Leaves drying strongly discolorous, dark above, pale below .

children.name: Rhaphidophora cryptantha P.C.Boyce & C.M.Allen
children.description: A species of extraordinary appearance, both in flowering in a neotenic state (otherwise known from R. hayi, R. parvifolia (Maluku) and R. pachyphylla) and especially by the inflorescences arising and opening on shoots carried behind the appressed shingling leaves. Often the mature inflorescences are completely obscured by the leaves, although occasionally the tip of the spathe is visible. In this

children.name: Rhaphidophora cylindrosperma Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Superficially similar to R. puberula but differing in leaves completely glabrous and never perforated, by the smaller, more slender spadix and in flowering on long, free shoots.

children.name: Rhaphidophora discolor Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: A remarkable and readily identifiable species with a large, very long-stipitate spadix. Confusion with Rhaphidophora stenophylla (also flowering on free shoots and with long-stipitate spadix) is possible, although the latter is readily identifiable by the much narrower leaf laminas, persistent petiolar sheath not degrading to strips and fibre, smaller (6-9 x 1.5-2.2 cm) spadix and long, pointed style

children.name: Rhaphidophora dulongensis H.Li
children.description: Lianas. Stem green, cylindric, 1–2m, 2–3cm in diam., internodes 0.5–2.5cm. Petiole 41–49 × ca. 1.5cm, basal 3–4cm sheathing; pulvinus indistinct; leaf blade pale green abaxially, green adaxially, oblong-ovate in outline, ca. 50 × 35cm, subleathery, base rounded or subcordate, pinnately divided; pinnae 6–9 per side, broadly linear, oblique, those at middle of leaf 4–5cm wide, apex truncate with falcate tip; costae 3 or 4, equally strong, parallel; sinuses nearly reaching midrib. Peduncle solit

children.name: Rhaphidophora elmeri Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Primary lateral veins on the abaxial leaf surface significantly more visible than interprimaries and never less than 5 mm apart. Spathe persistent during fruit development, eventually rotting away. Spadix 14-17 cm long Confusion with R. philippinensis is possible, although R. elmeri differs by flowering on clinging stems, in the proportionally narrower leaves (oblong rather than ovate), in the pr

children.name: Rhaphidophora floresensis P.C.Boyce
children.description: Petiole drying ± uniformly mid-brown, leaf lamina drying barely discolorous. Spadix slightly tapering-cylindrical; stigma punctiform, raised. Nusa Tenggara (Pulau Flores - endemic) One of a group of species that includes R. apiculata Engl. (New Guinea), R. hollrungii K. Krause (New Guinea), R. sabit P.C. Boyce and R

children.name: Rhaphidophora fortis P.C.Boyce
children.description: An extraordinary species with extremely stout, clinging flowering shoots and short-petioled leaves, the whole shoot resembling a plant of Bornean Scindapsus beccarii Engl.. Inflorescences are borne in the leaf axils. children.name: Rhaphidophora gorokensis P.C.Boyce
children.description: Similar to Rhaphidophora kokodensis, R. okapensis, R. pilosa and R. waria in being a montane species with small, stiffly coriaceous leaves. It is readily distinguishable from R. okapensis and R. waria by

children.name: Rhaphidophora guamensis P.C.Boyce
children.description: Rhaphidophora guamensis is a climbing plant in the family Araceae that is endemic to the island of Guam in the Mariana Islands.

children.name: Rhaphidophora hayi P.C.Boyce & Bogner
children.description: Rhaphidophora hayi is a species of flowering plant in the arum family Araceae, native to Queensland and New Guinea.

children.name: Rhaphidophora hongkongensis Schott
children.description: Lianas. Stem thick, rectangular in cross section; branches pendulous, 5–10 mm in diam.; internodes 1–4cm, rooting; internodes of juvenile branches elongated to 6–8cm, often producing aerial roots opposite to petiole. Petiole 5–10cm, sheathing to pulvinus; pulvinus conspicuous, 4–10mm; leaf blade pale green abaxially, green adaxially, usually falcate-elliptic, sometimes oblong-lanceolate, or oblanceolate, 20–35 × 5–6(–14)cm, base narrowly cuneate to minutely truncate, apex long acuminate; late

children.name: Rhaphidophora honkongensis Schott
children.description: Rhaphidophora honkongensis Schott is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora hookeri Schott
children.description: Nepal through NE India (type) to Bangladesh and Myanmar and N Thailand to N Laos and Vietnam.

children.name: Rhaphidophora intonsa P.C.Boyce
children.description: The densely netted fibre-encased shoot tips and large inflorescences are diagnostic. Confusion with R. spuria is possible although the latter is readily distinguished by the truncate to weakly cordate lamina base and in having very much less fibre at the shoot tips. Confusion with R. australasica is possible. Rhaphidophora intonsa differs by flower

children.name: Rhaphidophora intrusa P.C.Boyce
children.description: While resembling Rhaphidophora schlechteri, R. intrusa is immediately recognizable by the long extended spathe apex (up to 1/3 the length of the entire spathe) and by the greatly elongated petiolar sheath ligules that extend fused along the abaxial midrib for up to half the leaf lamina length. The latter character is also found, to a much lesser extent, in

children.name: Rhaphidophora jubata P.C.Boyce
children.description: A very distinct species notable for its overall large size, long peduncle and small stylar tops with prominently raised stigmas. Confusion with Rhaphidophora spuria is possible although the latter has larger stylar tops (1.6-2.4 x c. 2 mm diam.) and punctiform to slightly ellipsoid stigmas that are not prominently raised and do not dry glossy black, and ellipsoid seeds lacking a crest.

children.name: Rhaphidophora kokodensis P.C.Boyce
children.description: Superficially similar to Rhaphidophora australasica but readily separated by its flowering on free lateral shoots, by the flat-topped styles and the smaller, narrower, much more coriaceous leaves. In addition, being a montane species, R. kokodensis is separated altitudinally. Confusion with R. pilosa (also flowering on free lateral shoots) is possible, although

children.name: Rhaphidophora korthalsii Schott
children.description: Rhaphidophora korthalsii is a flowering plant of species Rhaphidophora the family Araceae.

children.name: Rhaphidophora lacduongensis V.D.Nguyen & B.H.Quang
children.description: The native range of this species is Vietnam. It is a tree and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora lancifolia Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Assam to China (Yunnan, W. Guangxi). It is a climber and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora latevaginata M.Hotta
children.description: Leaves always shingling, even in flowering individuals; leaf lamina stiffly coriaceous, broadly oblong-ovate-elliptic, 8-48 x 6.5-20.5 cm, bright green, slightly to markedly glaucous, base truncate-cordate to broadly cuneate. Flowering on clinging shoots.

children.name: Rhaphidophora lobbii Schott
children.description: Peninsular Malaysia (Kedah, Malacca, Pahang, Perak, Selangor, Terengganu), Singapore, southern Thailand, Sumatera, throughout Borneo extending to the Philippines (Palawan), and Sulawesi.

children.name: Rhaphidophora loricata Sowerby
children.description: Rhaphidophora loricata Sowerby is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora luchunensis H.Li
children.description: Lianas. Juvenile stems dark green, rooting, creeping on humus soil of forest understories or over bark mosses on trees, back rounded, moniliform or torulose, internodes thickened, 10–20 × 5–7mm. Petiole 20–25cm; sheath caducous, membranous; pulvinus ca. 10mm; leaf blade light green abaxially, green adaxially, black-brown when dry, ovate or ovate-lanceolate, 10–27 × 5–12cm, subleathery, base obliquely rounded, apex acuminate or caudate, unequally pinnately lobed; pinnae 2 or 3 on each side, or

children.name: Rhaphidophora maculata Harris
children.description: Rhaphidophora maculata Harris is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora megaphylla H.Li
children.description: N Thailand, N Laos, N Vietnam, SW China (type).

children.name: Rhaphidophora microspadix K.Krause
children.description: Rhaphidophora microspadix appears to be allied to R. neoguineense, differing in the much narrower leaf lamina with a long acuminate tip and in flowering habitually on long, pendent shoots.

children.name: Rhaphidophora mima P.C.Boyce
children.description: Papua New Guinea (Bougainville, Manus), Solomon Islands (Fauore, Guadalcanal, Kolombangara, Malaita, San Jorge, Small Malaita).

children.name: Rhaphidophora mirabile N.E.Br.
children.description: Rhaphidophora mirabile N.E.Br. is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora moluccensis Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Maluku. Endemic, known only from the type.

children.name: Rhaphidophora monticola K.Krause
children.description: A species of extraordinary appearance immediately recognizable by the texture and dense venation of the leaf laminas and by the remarkably elongated and robust peduncle, the latter being unique in the genus. It is not at all clear to what R. monticola is related.

children.name: Rhaphidophora neglecta A.Hay & P.C.Boyce
children.description: The native range of this species is New South Wales. It is a climber and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora nicolsonii P.C.Boyce
children.description: In general aspect R. nicolsonii resembles R. tetrasperma but is readily distinguished by the larger, considerably more coriaceous leaves, by the petiolar sheath extending to, at most, three quarters along the length of petiole and in the larger spadix and rounded stylar region. If the inflorescence of R. nicolsonii proves to be solitary per floweri

children.name: Rhaphidophora okapensis P.C.Boyce & Bogner
children.description: A very distinctive species notable for the stiffly erect, densely leafy stems, the thickly coriaceous, ovate-cordate leaves with a long acuminate tip, the relatively large inflorescences turning purple at maturity, the long-stipitate spadix, and the conical stigmatic region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora pachyphylla K.Krause
children.description: Long confused with Rhaphidophora hayi,R. pachyphylla differs in leaf shape, and form of the stigma. Additionally, R. pachyphylla lacks the disarticulating shoots unique to R. hayi, and never has foraging shoots.

children.name: Rhaphidophora petrieana A.Hay
children.description: Rhaphidophora petrieana A.Hay is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora philippinensis Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Immediately recognizable by the large, circular, raised stigma almost concealing the stylar region and by the prominently decurrent spadix. Confusion is possible with R. monticola which has similar leaf lamina texture and venation but may be readily distinguished by flowering on clinging stems, in the flat stigmas and in drying pale yellow-brown.

children.name: Rhaphidophora pilosa P.C.Boyce
children.description: Rhaphidophora pilosa is one of several montane species with stiffly coriaceous leaves (Okapensis Group). It is most similar to R. gorokensis and R. kokodensis, differing from the former in possessing fibrous shoot tips (R. gorokensis lacks fibre) and from the latter in the felted (not simply fibrous)

children.name: Rhaphidophora sabit P.C.Boyce
children.description: Potentially confusable with R. oligosperma (Maluku) but immediately distinguished by the much narrower, strongly falcate leaves, the sessile spadix and conical style.

children.name: Rhaphidophora schlechteri K.Krause
children.description: In most of its medium to large manifestations R. schlechteri is similar in overall appearance to R. mima, but is distinguishable by the marcescent spathe and stipitate spadix. Small forms of R. schlechteri maybe confused with R. neoguineensis , although the globose spathe and sessile ellipsoid spadix

children.name: Rhaphidophora schottii Hook.f.
children.description: Rhaphidophora schottii Hook.f. is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora sonlaensis V.D.Nguyen & P.C.Boyce
children.description: The native range of this species is Vietnam. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora spathacea Schott
children.description: Most similar to Rhaphidophora versteegii but readily separated by the non-shingling juvenile phase and on drying the strongly discolorous leaf laminas of which the abaxial surface is bright orange-brown with copious, minute tannin cells. Further, R. spathacea never has perforated leaf laminas.

children.name: Rhaphidophora stenophylla K.Krause
children.description: Unmistakable by the long, narrow leaves, persistent winged petiolar sheath, long stipitate spadix and prominently raised stigma. There exist plants with broader laminas than typical (Brass 27691 & 28311 are of this broad-leaf type) that may be confused with Rhaphidophora discolor (also flowering on free shoots and with long-stipitate spadix), although the latter is readily distinguished by the broader leaf laminas, petiolar sheath degrading to

children.name: Rhaphidophora stolleana Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: In its growth form, with long pendent stems with abbreviated flowering shoots arising in the leaf axils, Rhaphidophora stolleana resembles R. brevispathacea. The inflorescences are, however, quite different, with the spathe ovoid-cylindrical, 3-4 cm long, spadix slender cylindrical, 2.9-3.4 cm long in R. brevispathacea v. the spathe c. 10.2 cm long

children.name: Rhaphidophora teysmanniana Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Spadix not more than 3 cm long at anthesis. Sulawesi (endemic) Similar to R. neoguineensis and R. peekelii Engl. & K. Krause (both New Guinea, Bismark Archipelago, New Ireland, New Britain, Solomon Is.) but differing in the cylindrical rather than globose to elongate-globose spathe and the cylindrical, not ellipsoid, spadix.

children.name: Rhaphidophora todayensis K.Krause
children.description: Distinctive in the Philippines by the pubescent abaxial surface to leaf lamina and by the clusters of inflorescences subtended by and interspersed with thick fibrous cataphyll remains. The leaf pubescence recalls R. foraminifera (Sumatera, Peninsular Malaysia and throughout Borneo), R. puberula (Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatera, Nusa Tenggara and throughout Borneo) and

children.name: Rhaphidophora tonkinensis Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Vietnam. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora typha P.C.Boyce
children.description: The native range of this species is Borneo. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora ustulata P.C.Boyce
children.description: Petiole drying pale with apical geniculum much darker , leaf lamina drying strongly discolorous, pale yellow-brown abaxially, mid-brown adaxially. Spadix strongly tapering-cylindrical; stigma discoid, flat. Sumatera (Pulau Enggano - endemic). Distinctive in herbarium specimens by the strongly discolorous leaf lamina, the pale petioles and the dark apical geniculum. Rhaphidophora ustulata is most similar to R. floresensis from which it differs b

children.name: Rhaphidophora versteegii Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: Rhaphidophora versteegii is most similar to R. spathacea in having clusters of inflorescences subtended and interspersed by chartaceous prophylls and cataphylls. It is readily identifiable, and distinguished from R. spathacea, by the distinctive pale grey-green colour of dried material and the form of the juvenile growth phase. Further, leaf lamina

children.name: Rhaphidophora waria P.C.Boyce
children.description: Based on inflorescence presentation, Rhaphidophora waria is close to R. spathacea but differs in the smaller, narrower, much stiffer leaf laminas with the primary lateral and interprimary veins clearly differentiated from one another, the stipitate spadix and the deeply excavated stigmas.

children.name: Rhaphidophora microperforata
children.description: Rhaphidophora microperforata is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora muluensis
children.description: Rhaphidophora muluensis is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora acuminata
children.description: The native range of this species is Philippines. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora africana
children.description: Plant crawling at first, then climbing up to 10-12 m tall, then epiphytic; roots aerial, these are nodal, vertical and keep contact with the ground, the others are internodal or clamping, horizontal, 3-7cm long; stem thick, 0.5-1.5cm diameter when dry. LEAVES with petioles 15-27 (-35) cm, flattened on one face, enlarged at the base, bulging and often striate transversely at the apex; leaf blade 20-40 (-50) x 8-11 (-15) cm, thick, assymetric, oblong to lanceolate, base acute, decurrent on the

children.name: Rhaphidophora beccarii
children.description: The native range of this species is Arunachal Pradesh, Andaman Is., Pen. Thailand to W. Malesia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora burkilliana
children.description: The native range of this species is Pen. Malaysia (Selangor). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora calophyllum
children.description: Rhaphidophora calophyllum is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Rhaphidophora chevalieri
children.description: The native range of this species is N. & NE. Thailand to Vietnam. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora conica
children.description: Stylar region conical. Primary lateral veins drying much paler than abaxial leaf lamina. Indonesian Papua (Kepala Burung & Mimika Prov.), Papua New Guinea (Muyua, New Britain).

children.name: Rhaphidophora conocephala
children.description: Very close to and possibly indistinguishable from R. sylvest ris but consistent in the conical style topped with a prominent, raised button-like stigma and the notably more coriaceous leaves.

children.name: Rhaphidophora crassifolia
children.description: Leaf lamina thickly coriaceous to almost fleshy, falcate-elliptic-lanceolate to falcate-oblong or falcate-oblanceolate, 4.5-25.5 x 1.5-5 cm; margins slightly reflexed, this becoming greatly accentuated in dried material. The similar R. maingayi Hook.f. may be distinguished by the shoot apices covered with persistent untidy fibre derived from the degraded prophylls, cataphylls and petiolar sheaths.In the field the shoot apices distinguish

children.name: Rhaphidophora dahlii
children.description: The native range of this species is Bismarck Arch.. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora decursiva
children.description: Rhaphidophora decursiva is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Rhaphidophora elliptifolia
children.description: Confusion with R. elliptica is possible, although the smaller inflorescences and persistent fibre at the shoot tips readily distinguishes R. elliptifolia. Rhaphidophora elliptifolia resembles Peninsular Malaysian/Sumateran R. maingayi (see Boyce, 1999) in the persistent fibrous remains at the tips of

children.name: Rhaphidophora falcata
children.description: Recognized as distinct, despite the dearth of material and information, due to the falcate, stiffly coriaceous leaves, unique in the genus.

children.name: Rhaphidophora foraminifera
children.description: Rhaphidophora foraminifera is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Rhaphidophora formosana
children.description: The native range of this species is Taiwan. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora geniculata
children.description: The native range of this species is New Guinea. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora glauca
children.description: Nepal through NE India (type & type of R. glauca var. khasiana] to Bangladesh and Myanmar and N Thailand to N Laos and Vietnam.

children.name: Rhaphidophora koordersii
children.description: Leaf lamina on flowering shoots elliptic-lanceolate to oblong-elliptic, stiffly coriaceous, base cuneate, apex acuminate to attenuate with a prominent tubule. Sulawesi (endemic) Superficially similar to the widespread R. montana, Bornean R. elliptica Ridl. and R. elliptifolia Merr., but readily distinguished by the prominently stipitate spadix, rai

children.name: Rhaphidophora laichauensis
children.description: Lianas. Stem 1–2cm in diam., internodes 3–4cm, branched. Petiole ca. 30 cm, sheathing; pulvinus ca. 15mm; leaf blade broadly ovate, ca. 35 × 25–30cm, leathery, base truncate in outline, pinnately divided; pinnae 3 or 4 on each side, linear-oblong, ca. 14 × 3–4cm, apex falcate-truncate with ascending falcate tip, with 1 or 2 equally parallel costae, sinuses almost reaching midrib. Peduncle 15–18cm × ca. 5mm. Spathe yellow, 10–11.5cm. Spadix sessile, cylindric, ca. 11 × 1.5–2cm. Ovary hexagonal

children.name: Rhaphidophora liukiuensis
children.description: The native range of this species is S. Nansei-shotō to Taiwan (Lan Yü). It is a climber and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Rhaphidophora maingayi
children.description: Apices of active stems with netted prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath Rhaphidophora maingayi is virtually indistinguishable from R. montana (q.v.) but for the presence of very sparse to copious netted prophyll, cataphyll and petiolar sheath remains at the shoot apices. While this seems a weak character is does serve to distinguish the species in habitat and, indeed, R. maingayi and

children.name: Rhaphidophora megasperma
children.description: Distinctive in Borneo by the short leafy free side shoots bearing clusters of inflorescences subtended and interspersed by prominent chartaceous prophylls and cataphylls and by the spathe drying and persistent into early fruiting. children.name: Arophyton
children.description: Arophyton — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Arophyton buchetii Bogner
children.description: Rhizomatous plant; leaf blade always cordate, pale green, 20-50 x 18-35cm; synandriums dense on the male zone of the spadix; berries club-shaped to pyriform.

children.name: Arophyton humbertii Bogner
children.description: Rhizomatous; leaf blade with up to 7 segments, green on the lower surface; length of the spathe 1.2 times the spadix; spadix free with a long appendix; no sterile flowers.

children.name: Arophyton pedatum Buchet
children.description: Tuberous, leaf blade with up to 9 segments, glaucous on the lower surface; spathe 4 times as long at the spadix; female zone shortly joined with the spathe (for 1/4-1/4 of the length); no appendix; sterile flowers present between male and female zones.

children.name: Arophyton simplex Buchet
children.description: Leaf blade always hastate, with 3 (-4) primary lateral veins each side, whitish, of which only the upper two run very rapidly towards the apex; appendix slender, 3-3.5 cm long; sterile flowers between the male and female zones, style long.

children.name: Arophyton crassifolium
children.description: Tuberous plant, leaf blade cordate to subsagittate, 8-16 x 5-11 cm; synandrium sparse on the male zone of the spadix; berries ± elliptic.

children.name: Arophyton rhizomatosum
children.description: Leaf ± hastate (sometimes ± cordate) with all the transitions to a tripartite leaf ; appendix ca. 1cm long, ± fluted; male and female zones directly superposed, sometimes bisexual flowers in between the two.

children.name: Arophyton tripartitum
children.description: The native range of this species is NE. Madagascar. It is a rhizomatous geophyte and grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Culcasia
children.description: Culcasia — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Culcasia angolensis Welw. ex Schott
children.description: Leaves elliptic or elliptic-oblong, very obtuse at the base, 4-7 1/2 inches broad; peduncles 2 1/4-3 1/2 inches long.

children.name: Culcasia brevipetiolata Bogner
children.description: Planta scandens, glabra; internodia longa; petioli relative breves (1.8 – 2.6 cm longi), vagina longa (1.8 – 2 cm longa) et lata (0.4 – 0.5 cm lata); lamina foliorum ovata, basi rotundata et apice cuspidata; ovaria depresse globulata, stigma sessile; flos masculinus 3 – 4 staminibus instructus. Aliae species scandentes petiolis brevibus instructae a specie nova laminis foliorum rotundatis (Culcasia rotundifolia), laminis foliorum anguste ellipticis (C. lanceolata), laminis foliorum late ovati

children.name: Culcasia glandulosa Hepper
children.description: C. glandulosa appears to be quite distinct from any species of Culcasia so far described by the remarkable number of linear glands immersed in the tissues of the lamina which may appear as black or pellucid streaks. children.name: Culcasia linearifolia Bogner
children.description: Planta terrestris non scandens, erecta, radicibus rigidis; petioli breves (2 – 2.5 cm longi), vagina apice acuta; lamina foliorum linearis interdum subobliqua, 16 – 24 cm longa et 1.8 – 3 cm lata, basi cuneata, apice acuta; baccae depresse globulatae; semina ovoidea vel ellipsoidea, testa scabra. Culcasia linearifolia differt a speciebus ceteris generis lamina foliorum lineari.

children.name: Culcasia longevaginata Engl.
children.description: The native range of this species is Guinea to Ivory Coast. It is a subshrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Culcasia longivagina hort. ex Gentil
children.description: Culcasia longivagina hort. ex Gentil is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Culcasia orientalis Mayo
children.description: This species is confined to humid evergreen forests at lower altitudes in eastern Kenya and Tanzania. The few specimens seen from Pemba and Zanzibar differ from mainland collections in having inflorescences in groups of only 2 to 3, but agree in other respects.

children.name: Culcasia panduriformis Engl. & K.Krause
children.description: This species appears to be close to Culcasia dinklagei, but is distinguished by the truncate or cordiform base of the blade, the indistinct petiole and especially by the network of slightly prominent and elongated veins and veinlets, the primary veins are oblique towards the blade margin.

children.name: Culcasia reticulata hort. ex Gentil
children.description: Culcasia reticulata hort. ex Gentil is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Culcasia rotundifolia Bogner
children.description: LEAVES: Juvenile plants erect, with wide elliptic leaf blades and short internodes; adult plants scandent, with circular leaf blades and long internodes. Internodes in adult plants 3-7 cm long and 1-1.5 cm in diameter, slightly tinged with red, with [roots that adhere/stick] on[/from] the stem[/or stalk], these 0.5-1 cm long, more or less reddish. Petiole 0.8-1.5 cm long and 1-1.5 mm in diameter, reddish, flattened at the top with both margins somewhat raised. Blade 0.7-1 cm long, reddish, en

children.name: Culcasia seretii De Wild.
children.description: It seems logical to put in synonymy the 2 species Culcasia bequaertii De Wild and Culcasia seretii De Wild, with Culcasia sapinii De Wild; They have a number of characters in common: Prominent loops of the collective vein; filiform petioles and peduncles; short sheath, not surpassing 5 mm; interrupted branching of veinlets inside the mesh. Hepper (l.c., 1967) differentiated Culcasia seretii from Culcasia sapinii based on the length of peduncles and the s

children.name: Culcasia sapinii
children.description: Culcasia sapinii is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Culcasia tepoensis
children.description: Culcasia tepoensis is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Culcasia mannii
children.description: South-East Nigeria, Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea. In Cameroon, this species was collected in the regions of Nkongsamba, Limbe, Kribi, Ebolowa, Sangmélima.

children.name: Culcasia scandens
children.description: Culcasia scandens is an African climbing plant, often epiphytic, with slender, wiry stems, up to 5 m long clinging to tree trunks by means of clasping roots, and growing on forest and stream margins and in savanna.

children.name: Culcasia dinklagei
children.description: Forest zones, from Guinea to Congo; Common in Gabon and Cameroon where this species occurs generally in riparian forest zones (Kribi, Loldorf, Yabassi, Douala, Sangmélima, Abong, Mbang, Bertoua, Batouri, Yokadouma), in shaded, humid understorey or swamps.

children.name: Culcasia lanceolata
children.description: Species dispersed in Cameroon, in evergreen forest and semideciduous forest; Rare in Gabon, not found from other areas.

children.name: Culcasia parviflora
children.description: From Guinea to Congo and Bas-Zaire; Common in Gabon and Cameroon where the species occurs in evergreen forst (Nkongsamba, Kumba, Limbe, Kribi/ Eséka, Yaoundé).

children.name: Culcasia striolata
children.description: This species is rare from Guinea to Gabon. In Cameroon, it is more frequent in evergreen forest in the regions of Mamfé to Limbe (=Victoria), Douala, Yabassi, Edéa, Kribi.

children.name: Culcasia yangambiensis
children.description: The native range of this species is WC. Trop. Africa. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Culcasia annetii
children.description: This species, in a dry state, approaches Culcasia simiarum Ntépé-Nyamè by its ± oblique blade, subpeltate base and the lower surface with numerous small circular excrescences; but it differs by the petioles and peduncles being clearly shorter, and especially by the presence of a fine translucent network in the leaf parenchyma.

children.name: Culcasia bosii
children.description: This species approaches, by the foliar glands, Culcasia glandulosa Hepper from Western Africa, but it differs in the relative length of the petioles and peduncles, the shape of the blades and the structure of the inflorescence.

children.name: Culcasia caudata
children.description: LEAVES: Stem rather slender creeping and rooting, internodes 4-5 cm long, 2 mm thick, longitudinally sulcate. Petiole 1.5 x shorter than the blade, sheathed for 1/3 the length, 5-6 cm long. Blade thin, elongate-lanceolate, somewhat unequal, caudate with a tail like appendage-accuminate, 12-15 cm long, 2.5-3 cm wide, acumen 2 cm long, base 2-3 mm wide. primary lateral veins ca. 6-7 patent on each side, joined into a collective vein 2 mm from the margin. Cataphylls linear, sheath 2-2.5 cm long.

children.name: Culcasia ekongoloi
children.description: By the minute stigma, the frequent sympodial branching of the finely (‘tubéreuse’) [verrucose] stem, the ascending venation, this species is very close to Culcasia insulana, but it differs principally by the existence of a network of holey parenchyma, and by the stipitate spadix.

children.name: Culcasia falcifolia
children.description: The spathe appears to be thicker and usually larger than in C. orientalis, and its colour at anthesis also seems to be different; more field observations are needed.

children.name: Culcasia insulana
children.description: Bioko, Cameroon, Zaire and probably in Centrafrique. In Cameroon, this rare species has been collected in the regions of Mamfe, Kumba and Buea, in damaged forest understorey.

children.name: Culcasia liberica
children.description: Plant climbing 4-10 m, Anchor roots 2 cm long. LEAVES : Petiole 5-12 cm, sheath 1/3- ½ of petiole; Blade ovate-elliptic, apex acute or acuminate, coriacious, waxy, with lateral veins invisible on the upper surface, glossy; Secretory canals longitudinal to 1 cm long and dark punctate; Blade 19-26 cm long, 6-11 cm wide. children.name: Culcasia loukandensis
children.description: Cameroon, Gabon, Zaire (Mayombe). In Cameroon, this species, rare, occurs in the regions of East, Yaoundé and Kribi.

children.name: Culcasia obliquifolia
children.description: Gabon and Cameroon where the species was collected uniquely in the region of Kribi.

children.name: Culcasia sanagensis
children.description: This species approaches Culcasia barombensis because of its often parallel primary veins, the deep nework translucent in the mesh of veinlets, the spathe constricted towards the base, the bilocular ovary; It differs by the acute base of the blade, decurrent on the petiole, the densely verrucose stem , the short peduncles, the exserted spadix, and the plants ability to flower at less than 2 m above the ground.

children.name: Culcasia simiarum
children.description: This species, by its collective vein, approaches Culcasia tenuifolia Engl. and by the very slender, short sheath appraoches Culcasia seretii De Wild., but it differs by the clearly assymetric blade, not decurrent on the petiole, by the near or total absence of translucent dashes, by the blurred presence of a very fine network in the mesh of veinlets; in addition the petioles are not long, not fil

children.name: Culcasia tenuifolia
children.description: From Sierra Leone and Ivory Coast and Centrafrique to Gabon. In Cameroon, this species has been collected in the forest zones of the regions Nkongsamba, Kumba, Douala, Kribi, Eséka, Ambam, Djoum, Yokadouma, Moloundou.

children.name: Chlorospatha
children.description: Chlorospatha — a genus of liliopsidas.

children.name: Chlorospatha amalfiensis Croat & L.P.Hannon
children.description: Flowering is known to occur in Chlorospatha amalfiensis only during the month of February.

children.name: Chlorospatha antioquiensis Croat & L.P.Hannon
children.description: Chlorospatha antioquiensis is endemic to the eastern and western slopes of the Cordillera Central in Antioquia Dept., Colombia, to the north and south of Medellin, at 1,800-3,000 m elevation, 3,000 m being the highest elevation recorded for the genus.

children.name: Chlorospatha bayae Croat & L.P.Hannon
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a perennial or subshrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Chlorospatha besseae Madison
children.description: The native range of this species is NW. Ecuador. It is a perennial or subshrub and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Chlorospatha betancurii Croat & L.P.Hannon
children.description: Chlorospatha betancurii is known only from the eastern slopes of the Cordillera Central in Antioquia Department, Colombia, at 1,550-1,850 m elevation, a region with a high level of endemism in the genus.

children.name: Biarum pyrami
children.description: This large, showy species is perhaps the most readily distinguishable of the autumn flowering Biarum species due to the globose, strongly inflated, spathe tube, large spathe and greatly attenuated spadix appendix. The bullate leaves of the typical variety are also unusual in the genus and provide a ready means of identifying B. pyrami in Turkey, where no other species shares this character.

children.name: Biarum tenuifolium
children.description: Biarum tenuifolium is a cormous flowering plant species in the family Araceae.

children.name: Biarum davisii
children.description: Biarum davisii is an attractive species which, until the discovery of B. ditschianum , ranked as the most unusual taxon in the genus. Apart from its remarkably small size, characteristics such as the basically ovate foliage, deeply urceolate spathe tube, pinkish brown spathe and sweet lilac-like smell when in blossom are all unique in the genus.

children.name: Biarum ditschianum
children.description: Biarum ditschianum has a spathe limb reduced to a narrow rim on the spathe tube and the most notable feature is the relatively massive, dark yellow spadix appendix. Perhaps the most unusual feature of B. ditschianum is the presence of hair-like processes on the base of the spadix appendix. Such structures are otherwise unknown in the genus and are uncommon in the Araceae.

children.name: Biarum marmarisense
children.description: The native range of this species is E. Aegean Is. (Simi) to SW. Türkiye. It is a tuberous geophyte and grows primarily in the subtropical biome.

children.name: Biarum rhopalospadix
children.description: It may be readily distinguished by the lack of staminodes, the stigma borne on a short style, the narrow, parallel-sided spathe limb, and the considerably stouter spadix appendix.

children.name: Biarum aleppicum
children.description: From Biarum carduchorum and B . angustatum, B. aleppicum is readily distinguished by having the spathe tube margins free almost to the base and by the sessile stigmas. Biarum aleppicum has many more leaves than either B. angustatum or B. carduchorum, although the leaf shape approaches that of B. angustatum.

children.name: Biarum angustatum
children.description: It is outwardly very similar to B. carduchorum when in flower but is easily separated by the downward directed staminodes and narrower leaves with only 4 to 5 primary lateral veins per side. Another point of separation concerns the distribution of the species. Biarum angustatum is essentially a ‘ coastal ’ species, restricted to Syria and Israel. Biarum carduchorum is an inland species, distributed from south-eastern Turkey and north-western Syria through Iraq and into Iran.

children.name: Biarum carduchorum
children.description: Biarum carduchorum is most readily separated from B. angustatum by the upward-directed staminodes and the considerably wider leaves. B. carduchorum is found further inland than B. angustatum.

children.name: Biarum eximium
children.description: Biarum eximium differs from all other species of subgenus Ischarum in that the staminodes are evenly distributed over the entire length of the interstice between the male and female flower zones. Examination of a wide range of material of other species, particularly B. carduchorum and B. angustatum, revealed that although the main area of staminode distribution was directly above the pistillate flowers, in many individuals staminodes were present on the upper portion of the interstice, althou

children.name: Biarum crispulum
children.description: Since its publication Biarum crispulum has been universally treated as a synonym of B . bovei although B . crispulum is readily separable by its synantherous leaves, the narrow, incurved and heavily crispulate spathe margins, and a spadix appendix smelling of sour milk.

children.name: Biarum dispar
children.description: This interesting species has been much confused with the closely allied Biarum bovei from the eastern Mediterranean. It can be distinguished readily by the interstice which is approximately twice as long as the staminate flower zone, the presence of fewer and more scattered staminodes, and the narrower mature leaf blade. The overall size of the inflorescences has been used previously as a diagnostic feature, B. dispar having a smaller inflorescence than B. bovei.

children.name: Biarum olivieri
children.description: Biarum olivieri, is a curious species that is allied to B. bovei, B. dispar and B. crispulum but is separable by the linear to linear-lanceolate leaves, the much thinner, almost papery, spathe texture, the fully connate spathe tube margins and the filamentous spadix appendix. The floral odour produced by B. olivieri is also distinctive. Both B. dispar and B. bovei produce a dung like odour which, although unpleasant, is not nauseating; Biaru

children.name: Biarum straussii
children.description: Biarum straussii and B. syriacum are notable for having narrow, grass-like foliage and in producing inflorescences in early to mid-spring while the leaves are still present. Despite these similarities B. straussii is readily separated from B. syriacum by its broader leaves, presence of a style and the longer, narrower staminate flower zone.

children.name: Biarum syriacum
children.description: If the unusual flowering period is ignored, Biarum syriacum would appear, on the basis of floral morphology, to be related to B. bovei and B. kotschyi. The rather oblong spathe tube and the arrangement of the staminodes are similar to those of B. bovei. However, the foliage of B. syriacum is quite different and, in fact, no other species of Subgen. Ischarum have similar leaves.

children.name: Biarum carratracense
children.description: Biarum carratracense has been associated with B. bovei and B. tenuifolium but is quite clearly distinguishable from either. The oblong, slightly inflated spathe tube with the margins connate for over half their length and the fusiform spadix appendix suggest an affinity to B. kotschyi and B. fraasianum , although B. carratracense is geographically isolated from either species. Vegetatively B. carratracense would appear to be closest to B. kotschyi , which has a similar lanceolate-elliptic lea

children.name: Biarum kotschyi
children.description: Biarum kotschyi and B. carratracense are also similar. The rather slender spathe limb, fusiform spadix appendix and the arrangement of the staminodes is similar in both species. They can be readily distinguished by the degree of connation of the spathe tube margins (three quarters free in B. kotschyi, half free in B. carratracense) and their distinct geographical distributions.

children.name: Biarum fraasianum
children.description: Biarum fraasianum is most similar to B. bovei , B. kotschyi and B. carratracense , particularly in the degree of spathe tube inflation and the fusiform spadix appendix. The arrangement of the staminodes in B . fraasianum is closer to that found in B. dispar than to that of B. carratracense and B. kotschyi.

children.name: Biarum mendax
children.description: In herbaria, Biarum mendax has been assigned to B. bovei Blume, or B. dispar (Schott) Talavera, on the basis of its overall similarity to them. However, B. mendax is readily separable by its greater size, exceeding that attained by B . pyrami . Indeed, B . mendax is bears the largest infloresence yet recorded in Biarum . From all three species it can be distinguished by the completely fused spathe tube. Biarum mendax belongs to a group of species defined by spadices bearing sterile flowers on

children.name: Biarum auraniticum
children.description: Biarum auraniticum is unique in possessing a white spathe limb. There is no doubt that this is a most singular species, not only from the inflorescence coloration but also because of the remarkably wide bottle-shaped ovaries. The odd inflorescence coloration and unusual appearance of the ovaries make it difficult to envisage a close relationship. The lack of pistillodes, the ovate-elliptic, long-petiolate leaves and slightly inflated spathe tube support a link to B. bovei or B. kotschyi.

children.name: Philodendron bipinnatifidum Schott ex Kunth, 1841

children.name: Philodendron bomboizense Croat & Cerón

children.name: Philodendron bonifaziae Croat

children.name: Philodendron borgesii G.S.Bunting

children.description: Venezuela (Táchira), known only from the southern extreme of the Cordillera de Mérida at the headwaters of the Río Uribante basin, north of the Táchira depression.

children.name: Philodendron cannifolium Mart., 1831

children.name: Philodendron caracaraiense Croat
children.description: Philodendron caracaraiense is known only from Brazil but could be expected in southern Venezuela. It occurs on white sand soils in flooded campinas at about 200 m elevation probably in a Tropical moist forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron carajasense E.G.Gonç. & A.J.Arruda

children.name: Philodendron chrysocarpum Croat & D.C.Bay

children.name: Philodendron conforme G.S.Bunting

children.description: Apparently widespread in French Guiana, has been collected near the Surinam border at Crique Grégoire, and is to be expected in Surinam. This species is abundant everywhere in the vicinity of Eaux Claires near Saül in south-central French Guiana.

children.name: Philodendron planadense Croat
children.description: Philodendron planadense is known from the type locality near La Planada (hence the name P. planadense), Colombia (Narino), and also adjacent Ecuador (Carchi), at elevations of 1,750-2,265 m, in Premontane wet forest life zone. Apparently uncommon at La Planada, this species was collected in the regrowth forest along the trail above La Posada and in the swampy old pasture area south of the Sendero Natural, as well as in other sites not specifically described.

children.name: Philodendron platypetiolatum Madison
children.description: Ranges from Nicaragua to Ecuador. This species has been collected at several localities in Chocó and Valle Departments; in Ecuador, it has only been collected at and near the type locality.

children.name: Philodendron platypodum Gleason
children.description: French Guiana, Surinam, Guyana, Brazil (Amazonas, Bahia, Espirito Santo, Pará).

children.name: Philodendron pogonocaule Madison
children.description: Philodendron pogonocaule is a species of plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron pokigronense Croat
children.description: The species has no apparent close relatives but would key to Philodendron panduriforme (Kunth) Kunth which differs in having blades drying blackened with more deeply lobed margins and by having only 1-2 inflorescences per axil, or P. bipennifolium Schott which differs in being more deeply lobed and in having a single, much larger inflorescence.

children.name: Philodendron polliciforme Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron polliciforme must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although locally common in the Bajo Calima region, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron populneum K.Koch ex Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Trop. America (?). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron prancei Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Amazonas). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron profundisulcatum Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron prominulinervium Croat
children.description: Philodendron prominulinervium is endemic to Colombia (Narino), at elevations of 1,700-1,900 m, in Premontane wetforest life zone. This species has been seen several times at La Planada, including in the regrowth forest on the trail above "La Posada and along Sendero La Rosa to Potrero de Hermogenes.

children.name: Philodendron propinquum Schott
children.description: Brazil (Espirito Santo, Minas Gerais, Paraná, Rio de Janeiro).

children.name: Philodendron pseudauriculatum Croat
children.description: This species is recognized by its ap-pressed-climbing habit; short internodes; more or less rosulate habit; somewhat spongy, subterete petioles; oblong-elliptic to oblanceolate-elliptic, dark gray-green-drying blades with mostly narrowly rounded bases, and two to three inflorescences per axil; and white to pinkish spathes clearly demarcated from the peduncles. Philodendron pseudauriculatum is most easily confused with

children.name: Philodendron pseudoundulatum Grau
children.description: The native range of this species is Bolivia (Santa Cruz). It grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron pseudoverrucosum Croat
children.description: The species ranges from northern Ecuador to northern Peru at 284-1940 m but primarily between 1000 and 1400 m, occurring in Premontane wet forest and Premontane moist forest life zones. While most collections of the species have short pale lineations present on the upper surfaces, some collections appear to lack them all together. These are Foster 7732 (Peru, Pasco, Oxapampa), Asplund 18412 and Croat 58803 (Napo), Croat 99445 (Orellana), Croat 73480 (Pastaza) and (Napo).

children.name: Philodendron puhuangii Croat
children.description: Philodendron puhuangii is now known only from the type locality of La Planada, in Colombia (Nariiio), at elevations of 1,820-1,850 m, in Premontane wet forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron pulchrum G.M.Barroso
children.description: Ranges from Venezuela (Amazonas) to Colombia (Amazonas, Caqueta, Meta, Putumayo, Vaupes, Guania), Brazil (Amazonas), Ecuador (Napo, Pastaza, Morona-Santiago, Zamora-Chinchipe) and Peru (Loreto, Pasco, San Martín).

children.name: Philodendron purulhense Croat
children.description: Ranges from southern Mexico (Chiapas) to Guatemala (Alta Verapaz) and Honduras (Cortés and Olancho).

children.name: Philodendron pusillum E.G.Gonç. & Bogner
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron quelalii Croat & Mines
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron quinquelobum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Acre), Peru to Bolivia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rayanum Croat & Grayum
children.description: Spottily distributed from north-central Costa Rica to extreme eastern Panama.

children.name: Philodendron recurvifolium Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Bahia). It grows primarily in the seasonally dry tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron regelianum hort. ex Gentil
children.description: Philodendron regelianum hort. ex Gentil is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron reticulatum Grayum
children.description: Characterized by closely folded yellow-brown drying stems, nearly fully sheathed narrow petioles, narrowly elliptic blades which dry yellow-green below with prominent cross-veins giving the surface a prominent reticulate venation.

children.name: Philodendron rheophyticum Buturi & Temponi
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Paraná). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rhizomatosum Sakur. & Mayo
children.description: Vulnerable (VU) D2. Although it is protected in the Parque Nacional da Serra do Cipó, it can be considered as vunerable because of its specific habitat (forest patches), which may still be under pressure by wood extraction, local fires, visitor pressure and animal foraging.

children.name: Philodendron rhodoaxis G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is C. & S. Trop. America. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rhodospathiphyllum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron rhodospathiphyllum must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although locally common in the Bajo Calima region, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron ricaurtense Croat
children.description: Philodendron ricaurtense is apparently endemic to Colombia, known only from the type locality in Nariño Department near Ricaurte at 1100 m in a Premontane wet forest life zone.

children.name: Philodendron rigidifolium K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is SE. Nicaragua to Panama. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rimachii Croat
children.description: Planta terrestris; internodia brevia, 1-1.5 cm diam.; cataphylla viridia, (5.5-)7-13.5 cm longa, decidua; petiolus 11-43 cm longus; lamina triangulari-ovato-subsagittata, 18-38 cm longa, 5-22 cm lata; lobulis posterioribus 2.5-12 cm longis, nervis primariis lateralibus 3-8 utroque; inflorescentia 1-2 per quoque axillam, pedunculo 6-10 cm longo; spatha (4-)5.2-7.5 cm longa, tubo viride, lamina alba; spadix 6.7 cm longus.

children.name: Philodendron rio-pretense C.A.S.Bat. & M.L.Soares
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (NE. Amazonas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rodrigueziae Croat & Grayum
children.description: Known definitely only from the vicinity of the private ENDESA Reserve, established by the Corporatión Forestal Juan Manuel Durini near the town of Pedro Vicente Maldonado, Pichincha Province, Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron rodriguezii Croat
children.description: Philodendron rodriguezii Croat is a araceae species found in South America region.

children.name: Philodendron roezlii W.Bull
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron romeroi Grayum
children.description: Endemic to the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, Cesar and Magdalena Departments, Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron roraimae K.Krause
children.description: Not easily confused with any other, though it has leaf blades and cataphylls somewhat like larger plants of Philodendron chimantae. However that species differs in having a petiole which is usually conspicuously winged-angled, at least on the adaxial surface.

children.name: Philodendron roseocataphyllum Croat & M.M.Mora
children.description: Philodendron roseocataphyllum ranges along the Pacific slope of NW South America from Colombia (Choco) to Ecuador (Esmeraldas). At Cabo Corrientes it is occasional to common in the forest, usually occurring to 3 m high on trees.

children.name: Philodendron roseopetiolatum Nadruz & Mayo
children.description: Critically Endangered (CR), B1, a, b (i, iii); extent of occurence < 100 km 2. Only known from the type locality, where it was studied in the field by the first author. Subpopulations of this taxon are protected within the Reserva Ecológica de Macaé de Cima.

children.name: Philodendron roseospathum Croat
children.description: Ranges from Panama to Colombia. In Panama, this taxon is restricted to both sides of the Panama Canal, ranging from Veraguas to San Blas, mostly in Premontane rain forest or less frequently in Tropical wet forest life zones, at 350 to 1000 m elevation. In Colombia, it has been collected only in tropical pluvial forest at 100 to 900 meters.

children.name: Philodendron rothschuhianum  Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from Honduras (Gracias a Dios) and from Nicaragua (Río San Juan, Zelaya, Jinotega and Matagalpa) to Panama (Bocas del Toro, Veraguas, and Coclé), principally on the Atlantic slope.

children.name: Philodendron rubioi Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron rubromaculatum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron rubromaculatum must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). There is no reason to assume that it is exceedingly rare because only a tiny fraction of the Bajo Calima region has been studied, but it has not been collected elsewhere from other sites in Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron rubrum
children.description: Philodendron rubrum is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron rugapetiolatum Croat & M.M.Mora
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron ruthianum Nadruz
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Espírito Santo). It is a climbing epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sabaletense Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron samayense G.S.Bunting
children.description: Venezuela (Bolívar: Dtto Roscio).

children.name: Philodendron sanmarcoense Croat
children.description: Philodendron sanmarcosense is known only from type locality in Carchi Province of Ecuador near the Colombian border at 740 m in a Premontane wet forest life zone. It is expected to be found in adjacent Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron santodominguense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is NW. Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron scalarinerve Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron scherberichii Croat & M.M.Mora
children.description: Planta hemiepiphytica, ad 1.5 m; internodia 1.2-15 cm longa, 1.2-2.5 cm diam.; cataphylla ad 38 cm longa, debiliter 1-costata ad apex; petiolus (14-)30-40 cm longus, 3-7 mm diam., teres; geniculum ad 4 cm longum, 9 mm diam.; lamina anguste ovata-elliptica, (27-)45-60 cm longa, (9-)16.5-27 cm lata; nervis lateralibus (11-)17-21 utroque; inflorescentia solitaria pedunculo 3-3.5 cm longo; spatha 15.5-19.5 cm longa, 6 cm lata per anthesis, rubroviolacea vel marronina, sine constrictio; spadix pro

children.name: Philodendron schillerianum hort. ex K.Krause
children.description: Philodendron schillerianum hort. ex K.Krause is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron schmidtiae Croat & Cerón
children.description: Philodendron schmidtiae is currently known only from Ecuador but it is to be expected in adjacent Colombia (Putumayo) and in Peru (Amazonas). In Ecuador it is known from Sucumbios, Napo, Pastaza, Morona-Santiago and Zamora-Chinchipe, ranging from 450-2400 m. An unidentified collection from Peru (A. Monteagudo et. al. 13658) from the Parque Nacional Yanachaga-Chemillén at 2361 m is very similar but has blades that are matte rather than semiglossy on the upper surface.

children.name: Philodendron schottianum H.Wendl. ex Schott
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to Panama. In Panama, this species ranges no further east than Veraguas (Cerro Tute), except for a disjunct occurrence on Cerro Jefe in Panama Province. All Costa Rican collections are from the northern slopes of the Cordillera Central in Alajue-la, Heredia, and San Jose, and the northern end of the Cordillera de Talamanca in the Tapanti region of Cartago Province. It is to be expected throughout much of the Cordillera de Talamanca.

children.name: Philodendron schottii K.Koch
children.description: Occurs on the island of Jamaica and on the mainland from southern Mexico to east-central Panama, thence distinctly to southwestern Colombia and northwestern Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron scitulum G.S.Bunting
children.description: This species is totally distinct from P. auyantepuiense Bunt., differing by the proportionally broader leaf blade of thinner consistency with a few, more or less prominent, primary lateral veins. The latter species, known only from Auyantepui in the state of Bolivar, has a coriaceous (in vivo possibly somewhat fleshy) leaf blade with numerous, subequal lateral veins all manifest and a few primary

children.name: Philodendron scottmorianum Croat & Moonen
children.description: The conservation status for the species should be considered NT (Near threatened, IUCN 2001). Although the species is relatively common in the region where it was collected, it has not previously been collected in French Guiana or in adjacent countries.

children.name: Philodendron seguine Schott
children.description: Virtually endemic to Mexico where it ranges from central Veracruz to easternmost Chiapas. It has also been collected once in Guatemala.

children.name: Philodendron segunie
children.description: Philodendron segunie is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron senatocarpium Madison
children.description: North coastal Ecuador, with a seemingly disjunct population on the western slope of the Colombian Cordillera Occidental in Antioquia and Chocó Departments.

children.name: Philodendron sharoniae Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Colombia to Ecuador. It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron silverstonei Croat
children.description: The species is a member of Philodendron subg. Philodendron sect. Macrobelium subsect. Glossophyllum series Ovata and is recognised by its hemiepiphytic habit, thick stem with short internodes, deciduous cataphylls, subterete petioles, its large matte, ovate-sagittate leaf blades with a well-developed posterior rib and 10–12 pairs of basal veins, as well as by up to 5 inflorescences per axil with long peduncles, the spathe tube green outside, red-violet inside and with the spathe blade green o

children.name: Philodendron simmondsii Mayo
children.description: Philodendron simmondsii is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, endemic to Trinidad.

children.name: Philodendron simulans G.S.Bunting
children.description: The retention of the old cataphylls easily distinguishes this species from P. acutatum. Also, the nervature is inconspicuous, drying darker brown than the ground color of the blade, and' the primary lateral veins arise at a sharper angle. In P. acutatum, the veins are conspicuous, drying much paler than the base color of the blade, and the primary lateral veins originate at a wide angle (70-80°).

children.name: Philodendron sonderianum Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (S. Minas Gerais). It is a hemiepiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sousae Croat
children.description: The native range of this species is Mexico (Chiapas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sparreorum Croat
children.description: The species is recognized by its thick internodes, often longer than broad and drying with a smooth, light brown epidermis, as well as by its narrowly ovate-cordate blades with pale-drying major veins. More critical for recognition are the clusters of numerous, small, more or less pale orange inflorescences in one or more leaf axils, and especially the unusual pistils that have long, protruding, tapering styles.

children.name: Philodendron spec  K.Koch, 1855
children.description: Evergreen, small to gigantic, mostly climbing hemiepiphytes or epiphytes, sometimes arborescent to rhizomatous terrestrials; leaves with abundant resin canals; leaf blade very variable in shape, from linear to bipinnatifid, trisect or pedatisect, lacking a submarginal collective vein, fine venation parallel-pinnate; inflorescence secreting resin from spathe or spadix at anthesis; endothecium nearly always lacking cell wall thickenings; flowers unisexual, perigone absent; ovary usually 4-8-loc

children.name: Philodendron speciosum Schott, 1832
children.description: Philodendron speciosum, synonym Thaumatophyllum speciosum, is a species of plant in the family Araceae, native to Brazil and Bolivia.

children.name: Philodendron spiritus-sancti G.S.Bunting
children.description: Philodendron spiritus-sancti is a species of plant in the genus Philodendron native to the Brazilian state of Espírito Santo, which is the origin of its scientific name.

children.name: Philodendron splitgerberi Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Guianas, N. Brazil. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron spruceanum G.S.Bunting
children.description: Philodendron spruceanum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to southern Venezuela. It was first described by George Sydney Bunting in 1975.

children.name: Philodendron squamicaule Croat & Grayum
children.description: Philodendron squamicaule is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae.

children.name: Philodendron squamipetiolatum Croat
children.description: Ranges from Panama to Ecuador. In Panama this species is known only from along the Continental Divide in Cocle Province, whereas in South America it occurs along the Pacific slope of the Andes.

children.name: Philodendron stenophyllum K.Krause
children.description: The native range of this species is Peru. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron steyermarkii G.S.Bunting
children.description: The species is distinguished by its high climbing habit, long, slender internodes, terete petioles, the ovate-oblong blades with scarcely any development of primary lateral veins and with a sub-cordate base. The inflorescence is creamy, suffused with lilac outside on the tube and purple-magenta inside on the tube. Herbarium material is perhaps most easily confused with P. ptarianum, but the latter differs in having short internodes, a creeping

children.name: Philodendron straminicaule Croat
children.description: Known only from the Cordillera de Guanacaste in northwest Costa Rica and in western Panama, from Chiriqui and Bocas del Toro to Coclé Province.

children.name: Philodendron striatum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron striatum must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although locally common in the Bajo Calima region, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia.

children.name: Philodendron strictum G.S.Bunting
children.description: Ranges from Costa Rica to western Panama, Venezuela (Tachira), Colombia (Antioquia, Choco), and Ecuador (Carchi, Esrneraldas). In Costa Rica, this species occurs at 850 to 1525 m, and in Panama at 680 to 1665 m elevation in Lower Montane rain. Premontane rain, and Tropical wet forest life zones. In Colombia, this species has been collected at 100 to 150 m in Choco and Valle Departments, and in An

children.name: Philodendron suberosum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron suberosum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from six collections and has been found in both Chocó and Valle departments and many separate localities.

children.name: Philodendron subhastatum K.Krause
children.description: Ranges along the Pacific slope and adjacent lowlands of Colombia and Ecuador to the Provincias of Guayas and Chimborazo. In the Cabo Corrientes region it was collected from a semi-open area on the banks of Río Arusicito.

children.name: Philodendron subincisum Schott
children.description: Endemic to Mexico, known only from northern Veracruz in the Poza Rica region.

children.name: Philodendron sucrense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Sucre). It is a epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron sulcatum K.Krause
children.description: North-central Nicaragua through Costa Rica and Panama, thence discontinuously along the Pacific slope of South America south to Guayas and Chimborazo Provinces, Ecuador.

children.name: Philodendron sulcicaule Croat
children.description: Ranges from extreme southeastern Costa Rica to the Atlantic slope of Panama.

children.name: Philodendron swartiae Croat
children.description: The species is recognized by terrestrial habit, creeping stems, persistent cataphyll fibers, densely warty-verrucose-scaly petioles, and ovate-cordate blades. Philodendron swartiae is related to other members in an unnamed section and species in the group include P. pastazanum K. Krause and P. gloriosum André.

children.name: Philodendron tachirense G.S.Bunting
children.description: The species is recognized by its scandent habit, caducous, unribbed cataphyll, moderately spongy, more or less terete petioles, its ovate, inequi-laterally ovate, subcordate to cordate blades with a triangular sinus which is broader than deep and with the posterior rib not naked. Also characteristic are the inflorescences which occur in clusters of 4-5 per axil, have uncon-stricted spathes with the tubes green outside, maroon within and with the blades white on both surfaces.

children.name: Philodendron tatei K.Krause
children.description: Philodendron tatei K.Krause is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron teretipes Sprague
children.description: Affinities with Philodendron glaziovii Hook. f., distinguished from this by terete petioles, smaller subsessile inflorescence and fewer ovules.

children.name: Philodendron thalassicum Croat & Grayum
children.description: Ranges from central Costa Rica to western Panama (Chiriquí).

children.name: Philodendron thaliaefolium Schott, 1856
children.description: Philodendron thaliaefolium Schott, 1856 is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron thaliifolium Schott
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron theofiloanum Calazans
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Minas Gerais). It grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tortum M.L.Soares & Mayo
children.description: Philodendron tortum is a species of flowering plant in the family Araceae, native to northern Brazil and Bolivia.

children.name: Philodendron toshibae M.L.Soares & Mayo
children.description: The native range of this species is Brazil (Amazonas). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron toshibai M.L.Soares & Mayo
children.description: Philodendron toshibai M.L.Soares & Mayo is a araceae species found in South America region.

children.name: Philodendron triangulare G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Trujillo). It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tricostatum Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron tricostatum must be considered as Least Concern (LC) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001), since it is known from six collections and has been found in both Chocó and Valle departments and many separate localities.

children.name: Philodendron triplum G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela (Bolívar). It is a epiphyte and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron trojitense Croat & D.C.Bay
children.description: IUCN Red List category. Conservation for Philodendron trojitense must be considered as Near Threatened (NT) according to IUCN Red List criteria (IUCN, 2001). Although reasonably common in the area of the type locality, it is not yet known from other sites in Colombia. It is possible that the species is more widespread than is currently known because much of the Pacific slope is still poorly known.

children.name: Philodendron trujilloi G.S.Bunting
children.description: The native range of this species is Venezuela. It is a climber and grows primarily in the wet tropical biome.

children.name: Philodendron tuerckheimii Grayum
children.description: North-central Oaxaca and east-central Veracruz to extreme eastern Panama, south through the Colombian Cordillera Occidental to northwestern Ecuador, and east through the Colombian Cordilleras Central and Oriental and the Venezuelan Cordillera de Merida to the western end of the Cordillera de la Costa in Yaracuy State.

children.name: Philodendron tuxmog
children.description: Philodendron tuxmog is a araceae species found in its native region.

children.name: Philodendron tysonii Croat
children.description: Known only from Panama, but is expected to be found in the Cordillera de Talamanca of Costa Rica.

children.name: Philodendron ubigantupense Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, known only from the type locality along the Atlantic coast.

children.name: Philodendron urraoense Croat
children.description: Philodendron urraoense is a member of P. sect. Philodendron sect. Macrobelium subsect. Macrobelium and is characterised by its hemiepiphytic climbing habit, the internodes usually longer than broad and drying yellow-brown with longitudinal ridges, petioles subterete and shorter than blades and drying blackened, blades ovatecordate and drying somewhat blackened with a narrow, triangular sinus and with the basal veins free to the base or nearly so as well as by the cluster of up to 8 moderately

children.name: Philodendron ushanum Croat & Moonen
children.description: Planta hemiepiphytica; internodia adulta 3.5-6.5(-8) cm longa, 8-10 mm diam.; cataphylla 13-18 cm longa, 2-costata, persistentia semi-intacta; petiolus subteres, 17-19 cm longus, 1-1.3 cm diam.; lamina anguste ovata, 24-27 cm longa, 9-10 cm lata, nervis primariis lateralibus 4-6 utroque; inflorescentia solitaria, pedunculo 1.5-2 cm longo; spatha 10.5 cm longa, tubo 4.5-5 cm longo, 2 cm diam.; spadix 9 cm longus, parte pistillata 2.7 cm longa, 1.2 cm diam., pistillis 5-6-locularibus, ovulis 3-

children.name: Philodendron utleyanum Croat
children.description: Endemic to Panama, known only by the type specimen from Colón Province.

children.name: Philodendron ventricosum Madison

children.description: Philodendron adamantinum, synonym Thaumatophyllum adamantinum, is a plant in the genus Philodendron, in the family Araceae. It is native to South America, namely to Southeast Brazil, but is also cultivated as a houseplant in cooler climates.

children.name: Thaumatophyllum bipinnatifidum  Sakur., Calazans & Mayo
children.description: Philodendron bipinnatifidum, synonyms including Thaumatophyllum bipinnatifidum and Philodendron selloanum, (common names: split-leaf philodendron, lacy tree philodendron, selloum, horsehead philodendron, guaimbé) is a plant in the genus Philodendron, in the family Araceae. The species is native to South America, namely to Brazil, Bolivia, Argentina, and Paraguay, but is also cultivated as a landscape plant in tropical, subtropical and warm temperate climates.

The latter two species differ by having much more elongated blades whereas A. mateoi has ovate blades 17-18 cm long. In the Lucid Anthurium key, A. mateoi tracks with A. geniculatum Sodiro and A. karstenianum Engl. children.name: Anthurium monteagudoi
children.description: Anthurium monteagudoi is a member of sect. Xialophyllium. Its blade resembles some of the less typical blades of Anthurium valenzuelae also collected from Peru in this study. Anthurium monteagudoi is distinguished from A. valenzuelae in having fewer primary lateral veins (8-12 versus 11-21), distinctive collective vein pattern and a stipe that measures in cm rather than mm. Anthurium monteagudoi tracks in the Lucid Anthurium key with A. aristatum Sodiro, A. funiferum Klotzsch & H. Karst. ex E

children.name: Anthurium valenzuelae
children.description: A few blades of Anthurium valenzuelae that were wider than typical for the species were similar to A. monteagudoi but A. monteagudoi is distinguished by having fewer primary lateral veins (8-12 versus 11-21) and collective veins which emerge prominently from the base forming a straight-sided V for 4-6 cm to near the margin.

children.description: Heteropsis croatii is morphologically similar to H. robusta in the quadrangular internodes, oblanceolate leaf blade and inflorescence size, but differs by the midrib which is not yellowish on the lower surface in dried material, the adaxially impressed primary lateral veins, the thicker floral shoot axis, and especially by the short, usually extrorsely twisted peduncle and cuspidate spathe much longer than

children.name: Heteropsis duckeana M.L.Soares
children.description: Heteropsis duckeana is morphologically similar to H. rigidifolia from the Atlantic Forest but differs in the less coriaceous, non-rigid, and less spreading leaf blade, longer internodes and petioles, and especially in the larger size of the spadix and seeds. In H. rigidifolia the internodes are 1.5 – 2 cm long, the petiole 3 – 5 cm long, the leaf blade is coriaceous, rigid and spreading, the spathe is 2 – 2.5 cm long, the spadix 1.5 – 3 cm long, 0.6 – 0.8 cm diam. a

children.name: Heteropsis oblongifolia Kunth
children.description: Phenology — Flowering and fruiting specimens have been collected almost throughout the year, but specimens have not been seen in flower in June and September or in fruit in August.

children.name: Heteropsis peruviana K.Krause
children.description: Phenology — Flowering specimens have been collected in September and fruiting material from January to March, in July, and from October to November.

children.name: Heteropsis reticulata Croat & M.L.Soares

children.name: Heteropsis salicifolia Kunth
